# Xiuhtēcuhtli, translated into industries: what the archetype actually does
Every age hires the same gods; only the job titles change. **Xiuhtēcuhtli** never stopped working.

Xiuhtēcuhtli's myths are the calendar's: the fire that must be renewed, and the darkness that waits if it is not.

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) — which maps every flagship temple to the industries its archetype demonstrably resonates with, each match argued and open to challenge — seats this temple in **3 industries**. This file reads those seats the way they were earned: through the myths.
## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Xiuhtēcuhtli
- **Pantheon:** Nahuatl
- **Domain of influence:** Fire, Time, Hearth
- **Pattern seats:** 3
- **Sectors touched:** Culture & Entertainment · Energy & Natural World · Technology & Innovation
- **Strongest seat:** Timekeeping & Calendar Systems
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 265 of 271
## The Myth at Work

**The Drilling of the New Fire.** At the close of each 52-year cycle (xiuhmolpilli), the Aztec world extinguished every flame: households went dark, debts were settled, and the priests climbed Huixachtlan — Hill of the Star — to watch for the Pleiades' midnight passage.  On a captive's chest the fire-priest drilled the new flame; if it caught, the runner carried it to the Templo Mayor, and every hearth in the empire was relit from it. — hold that image; the industries below are where it goes to work.

**Huehueteotl, the Old One.** Under his other name he is the oldest thing in the cosmos: Huehueteotl, the wrinkled god who carries the brazier on his bent back, present before the suns.  The Aztecs put him at the center of the universe's four directions — the fire-pillar of the world — and every domestic hearth was his shrine: the smallest and the greatest cult at once, the god of the kitchen who is also the god of the calendar. — hold that image; the industries below are where it goes to work.
## The Seats

Each of these is argued in the atlas with a weight and a why-line. What the atlas cannot fit in one line is the whole myth — so here is each seat with its story restored.

### Timekeeping & Calendar Systems

*Watches, calendars, and time sciences. (Sector: Culture & Entertainment)*

*The 52-year New Fire cycle; time restarted by hand.* Swap the costume and the sentence is indistinguishable from the myth. That is what a resonance seat means.

### Thermal, Geothermal & Fire Energy

*Geothermal plants, combustion, and industrial heat. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

*The Aztec fire itself — first and last of the gods, the hearth at the center of the universe; heat made lord.* Swap the costume and the sentence is indistinguishable from the myth. That is what a resonance seat means.

### Manufacturing, Craft & Automation

*Fabrication, industrial craft, and robotics. (Sector: Technology & Innovation)*

*The fire-drill and the forge; the hearth of all making.* Swap the costume and the sentence is indistinguishable from the myth. That is what a resonance seat means.

Read the myth again after the seats and it stops sounding ancient: Xiuhtēcuhtli's myths are the calendar's: the fire that must be renewed, and the darkness that waits if it is not. The age changed. The work did not.
